1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line spacing and clear hierarchy across all screens, though letter-spacing does not appear extra-expanded.

2.why: No italics or all-caps body text appear; instructions are short phrases or single sentences without dense blocks.

3.why: Layouts are single-column, generously padded, and fit a mobile viewport with large tap targets and no horizontal overflow.

4.why: Copy such as “Start your security setup,” “Get a six-digit identity code,” and “There is no reading timer” is short and plain.

5.why: Demo credentials are shown on the login screen and the code field uses the placeholder example 123456.

6.why: Every screen contains only brief labels, one-sentence status banners, or short helper text; no long passages must be read.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard controls are present for the identity code (revealed only in the browser console) or other secrets.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is offered on any screen.

9.why: Standard email and password inputs are used, which browsers and password managers can autofill, though no explicit autocomplete attributes are visible.

10.why: A progress bar, bold step headings, and a single large blue primary button make the current step and main action obvious.

11.why: Each screen presents one primary action (Sign in, Get identity code, Check code) with secondary options clearly de-emphasized.

12.why: Green status banners explicitly state what just happened and what to do next after sign-in and code request.

13.why: A “Re-request identity code” button and the ability to re-enter and resubmit the code are provided with no penalty indicated.

14.why: The error “That code does not match. Check the six digits, or request a new code” names the problem and the fix without blame.

15.why: A banner states “There is no reading timer. Take as long as you need,” and no countdown or expiry is shown.
